title: Hugo and Bloom's Farm Surprise
markdown:
The sun painted the sky with morning light. Hugo, the toy fixer, walked with Bloom the bee. Hugo carried a little wooden robin with a droopy wing.

They came to Farmer McGregor’s farm, full of new life. Tiny chicks, like fluffy yellow seeds, cheeped close to Mama Hen. Ducklings bobbed beside their mother, webbed feet ready for paddling. Woolly lambs stood on sturdy legs, their horns not yet grown.

Miss Maple was mending a fence rail nearby. She lifted a hand, then left them to look. The farm smelled of hay and warm milk.

Bloom zipped, antennae curious. “Oh, Hugo. Why do the ducklings and lambs look so like their mamas already? The chicks are just soft puffs.”

Hugo knelt by clover, voice calm. “Ah, Bloom. Look closely. The chicks can walk, but they stay near the hen. Their fluff keeps them a little warm, and she keeps them a lot warm. They still need that huddle.”

Bloom imagined the chicks snuggled with Mama Hen. A pause. Clover bells. A calf’s ear flicked at a fly.

“And then,” Hugo smiled, “look at the ducklings. They already have webbed feet for the pond. The lambs already have legs for standing and woolly coats. They will still grow bigger. They are just born ready for the kind of life their family lives.”

Bloom’s wings fluttered. She watched a piglet nuzzle its mama. “So that piggy already has its snout for snuffling.” She saw a wobbly calf. “And that calf already has its strong legs.” The farm, she realised, was full of wonderful differences. Not some babies slow and some babies finished. Different kinds of ready.

Miss Maple wandered over with a tiny wooden peg. Hugo set the robin on the fence post and she helped him ease the droopy wing straight. A quiet click. The robin looked ready to be a robin again.

As the sun began to set, Hugo and Bloom journeyed home. The little robin rode safe in Hugo’s pocket, wing true. Bloom hummed. She told a ladybug resting on a grass blade. “Some babies stay close for warmth. Some already have the feet or coats they will use. All of them still grow.”

Nearing Hugo’s garden, Bloom felt happy curiosity bubble. “I wonder what other secrets the world is holding.”
characters: Hugo (a toy fixer), Bloom (a bee), Maple (a neighbour)
author: StoryGen Community
